name: coga-dev/principles
description: Coga's design principles — the shared foundation for developing Coga and writing its README.
---

# Coga's design principles

Coga is an instrument for people directing agents, not another coding
agent. Agents work in sessions; people's goals, questions, and decisions
outlive those sessions. Coga keeps the working plan in text people can
inspect, challenge, and change — including when the right decision is not
to build.

## Principles

- **Expand human capacity.** Expand people's ability to think, explore, and
  create. People choose purpose and direction; agents help discover problems,
  challenge assumptions, and build. Automate mechanical work to leave more
  attention for judgment. People and agents together do not outperform the
  stronger of the two by default; process makes the difference. Route each
  step to whoever is stronger at it, and keep the whole problem in a form
  people can see and restructure, so together they reach what neither reaches
  alone.
- **Text above code.** Readable text carries intent, knowledge, and decisions.
  Code implements that understanding and can be rewritten as we learn.
- **Context is explicit.** People can find, question, correct, and choose the
  knowledge each task needs. Make what an agent works from understandable.
- **Small improvements compound.** Correct the instructions behind an error
  so later work starts from better understanding. Keep changes visible and
  correctable; retain what proves useful and revise what stops working.
- **Yours and hackable.** People own their knowledge and tools. They can
  inspect, change, and move them, reshape how they work, and replace agents.
  The mechanisms serving those freedoms can change too.
- **Keep everything at human scale.** Keep Coga a thin overlay on agent
  capabilities, small enough to inspect and change. The tool should fit the
  way people work, not make them fit its process.
- **Amplify agents, don't duplicate them.** Use existing coding agents to
  plan, research, implement, and review. Coga organizes and carries their
  work across tasks and sessions instead of rebuilding their capabilities.
- **Coga encoded in Coga.** Use the same tickets, contexts, and workflows to
  describe and evolve Coga itself.
- **Fail loud.** Surface missing knowledge and failed operations so people
  can correct them. Never present an unnoticed failure as success.
- **The task outlives the session.** Give substantive work a durable record
  that people can direct and agents can resume.

## Consequences

- **Homoiconicity for agents.** Tickets, contexts, and workflows use the
  same Markdown that agents read and can edit. There is no separate
  agent-only version of the plan.
- **Everything is disposable except the text.** Code and methods can be
  replaced. Intent, decisions, and what we learn survive in editable files.
- **Agents can manage Coga itself.** They can write tickets, revise contexts,
  and change workflows without learning a special language.
- **Build Coga on base concepts agents are good with.** Use familiar tickets,
  plans, and workflows rather than inventing a language agents must learn.

## In practice

Planning serves both people and agents. The agent's proposal gives the human
something concrete to read: the intended outcome, assumptions, approach,
and criteria for success. A human can question its assumptions, correct the
tickets or context, add a review step, or stop the project. The revised text
also directs later agent work. Coga uses the agent's planning capability and
keeps that shared understanding editable across sessions. The
[Coga history examples](../../../../README.md#when-coga-changed-its-own-mind)
show a discarded architectural assumption and a maintenance workflow changed
when it became clear that transient notes would not preserve key findings.

Fresh sessions make written handoffs important. The agent records useful
findings, decisions, and open questions in the
[blackboard](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/blackboard/SKILL.md); the next
[launch](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/prompt-composition/SKILL.md) starts from the current
files. People can inspect, correct, and share the working knowledge carried
forward. The record can be incomplete or wrong, so its reviewability matters
as much as its persistence. This gives people a practical way to manage
context rot and understand the work they delegate.

Choose knowledge and procedures for their relevance to the task. Explicit
attachment puts selected guidance into the starting prompt; deciding what is
needed, missing, or obsolete remains work for people and agents. The
[research on context and skills](reading-list.md#context-skills-and-plan-review)
supports examining that choice carefully: useful guidance can help, while
irrelevant or conflicting instructions can add cost or hurt results. Those
studies do not establish a performance gain for Coga itself.

These principles guide Coga's design. The
[README](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/README.md) derives from them;
edits to the README must stay aligned. Behavioral topics own current
implementation contracts, including Git. The
[reading list](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/docs/contexts/coga-dev/principles/reading-list.md)
records our influences.

# Feature checkouts

Code-ticket work runs in the checkout the session was launched from. Every
session starts from a clean, current `main`, a step that changes code works
on its feature branch, and the session ends back on `main`. Under
`coga launch` the launcher performs the branch setup and both moves; in any
other session the agent does. Ticket work creates no linked worktrees; the
one alternative checkout is the [sandbox clone fallback](sandbox-clone/SKILL.md).
Only the recurring runner's temporary control worktree and Retro's isolated
checkout (created and removed for one Retro pass) are linked worktrees; ones
left from an earlier layout are disposed of by
[coga/checkout-cleanup](../checkout-cleanup/SKILL.md).

The ticket's `## Dev` record (`branch:`, `worktree:` for a sandbox clone,
`pr:`) is the link from ticket to branch to PR. It is explicit, not inferred
from the slug, because slug conventions break whenever a PR bundles tickets,
an agent picks another branch name, or a slug is truncated. Anything that
follows the link (bump gates, `open-pr`, autoclose, retire, status views)
reads the record; a branch name need not match the slug.

`origin` and `main` stand for the configured `[git].remote` and
`[git].control_branch`; `coga/tasks/`, `coga/recurring/`, and `coga/log.md`
for the configured workspace's task, recurring, and log paths. **The Coga
roots** are the Coga root plus the configured contexts root; every eligible (unignored) file there is Coga state
that publication carries ([coga/state-publication](../state-publication/SKILL.md)).

## Leaves

- [reconciliation](reconciliation/SKILL.md) — keeping edits current with main.
- [launch-boundary](launch-boundary/SKILL.md) — preparing and returning the
  invoking checkout, refusal recovery, and exemptions.
- [chat](chat/SKILL.md) — direct chat's occupancy guard and branch.
- [manual](manual/SKILL.md) — the start, work, and end an agent performs
  when launch did not prepare the branch.
- [sandbox-clone](sandbox-clone/SKILL.md) — the sandbox clone fallback.

Main can advance during any session. Follow

policy, including documentation, ticket edits, and ad-hoc work.

The frozen step declares its entry. A workflow step may set `checkout:` to one
of four values ([definition format](../workflows/SKILL.md#definition-format)):

- `create-or-reuse` — create the task branch, or reuse the recorded one.
- `reuse-required` — reuse the recorded `branch:`; refuse without one.
- `manual` — launch prepares and returns control but sets up no branch and
  says so; the agent follows this topic itself. An omitted field means
  `manual`.

Freezing writes the explicit value on every step, so a declared policy is
authoritative: workflow name, step name, skills, a local edit of the step's
skill or section, `assignee:` and `requires:` do not change it. Customize the
procedure and its instructions freely; the checkout follows the declaration.
The field is data for the shared mechanics below and never bypasses
occupancy, Git, owner-gate or assist checks. Roles and completion gates stay
independent: a `manual` step that `requires: branch` still needs its

Every frozen `checkout:` value is validated before launch reserves, creates or

initial normalization to control precedes that refusal. An invalid value,

refuses before spawning; retry it.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `code/design-then-implement` | `design`, `evaluate-design`, `review-design` | `control` |
| all five packaged code/docs workflows | `implement` | `create-or-reuse` |
| `code/agent-merge`, `code/design-then-implement`, `code/with-review`, `docs/with-review` | `peer-review` | `reuse-required` |
| `code/with-self-review` | `self-qa` | `reuse-required` |
| `code/agent-merge`, `code/design-then-implement`, `code/with-review`, `docs/with-review` | `open-pr` | `control` |
| `code/with-self-review` | `pr` | `control` |
| `code/agent-merge` | `merge` | `reuse-required` |
| all but `code/agent-merge` | owner-held `review` (an explicit assist) | `reuse-required` |

Every other packaged workflow omits the field and freezes `manual`.

their snapshots.

delegates to `code/peer-review`; both must match. Anything else gets

this path selected the entry.

No command rewrites a frozen ticket to add `checkout:`. The fallback may be
deleted only in a reviewed change after no live ticket in supported repos

reviewed migration of those snapshots. Do not rewrite snapshots merely to

An ordinary `coga launch` of an agent-held step (or an explicit assist on an

   Other managed paths retain independent linkage publication. Otherwise it reuses the first
   recorded `branch:`: a local ref as is (a behind one fast-forwards to its
   remote; ahead or diverged commits are kept and reported), or one created
   from its remote tip. It refuses — on control, starting nothing — a
   recorded branch absent everywhere, a reuse step with no branch (unless
   `## Already satisfied` evidence exists: the agent then verifies from
   control), a branch committing ticket intent control lacks ([stranded
   ticket writes](#stranded-ticket-writes)), one held by another worktree,
   or ignored files the switch would overwrite. After switching it projects
   only this ticket from control, unstaged: the session's only entry dirt.

   `commit -a`. Never stage, commit, or restore the projected ticket. A
   context, skill, or workflow edit that belongs to the code PR is committed
   with it. Left dirty, it is
   [held for merge](../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts):
   the sweep does not publish it, and return refuses until it is committed
   on the branch or redone on control.
   To rebase, first copy the ticket outside the repo and verify the copy,
   restore it from HEAD (delete it if HEAD lacks it), rebase, then write the
   copy back unstaged and compare bytes. Test, commit, rebase onto
   `origin/main`, push.

   The bump itself was recorded, so never bump again to publish it: after a
   `sync failed`, once Git access is restored, run the `coga run

   After a `sync refused` (control's ticket changed meanwhile), preserve the
   handoff and reconcile it onto control's copy
   ([reconciliation](reconciliation/SKILL.md)). An unused prepared branch
   needs no commit or PR when the work proves already satisfied.

branch by name from there. A step that must exceptionally change code from

# Manual start, work, end

Part of [coga/checkouts](../SKILL.md), which owns the launched lifecycle and
which checkout each step starts in.

## Procedure

Use this when no `COGA_LAUNCH_RETURNS_CHECKOUT=1` witness is set — manual or
API sessions, megalaunch picks, exempt checkouts — and before editing in a
step whose runtime notice says launch set up no branch (manual policy, or a
control step that must exceptionally change code). The agent performs both
moves:

1. **Start check.** `git fetch origin main`, then require HEAD on `main`, a
   clean tree with Coga state included, and a successful `git merge
   --ff-only origin/main`. Launch regenerates the ignored
   `coga/.agent-skills/` view; a repo initialized before `coga init` wrote
   that ignore rule sees it as dirt — add `.agent-skills/` to
   `coga/.gitignore`, never commit it. Anything else — dirty files, another
   ticket's branch, a diverged `main` — means stop: ask the attending human,
   or `coga block` in a queue run. Do not work around an occupied checkout
   with a linked worktree, a control checkout, a stash, or a switch.
2. **Work.** Write ticket state (`branch:` under `## Dev` once created with
   `git branch <name>`, plan notes) on `main`, publish it (below), then
   switch to the feature branch and change code only; ticket edits made
   there are not published until the next sweep. A resumed branch is reused:
   switch to it and `git rebase` onto fetched `origin/main`.
3. **End.** Commit, push the branch (`git push -u origin <branch>`, or
   `--force-with-lease` after a rebase), then return:
   - `git fetch origin main`;
   - for every dirty path under the Coga roots, verify it is already on
     `origin/main` by the rules of
     [the launch boundary](../launch-boundary/SKILL.md) (`git diff --quiet origin/main -- <path>`;
     for `coga/log.md`, every added line is on `origin/main`) and discard it
     (`git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <path>`). `git diff`
     skips untracked files, so compare an untracked one with
     `git show origin/main:<path> | cmp - <path>` and delete it only when
     identical;
   - `git switch main`, then `git merge --ff-only origin/main`.

   If any dirty path under the Coga roots is *not* already on `origin/main`,
   or any other path is dirty, stop and escalate. A knowledge file the sweep
   [held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
   belongs in the branch's commit (or redone on `main`), not discarded. Never discard unpublished
   state. Then write the step's handoff on `main` and run `coga bump`, which
   publishes it. The session leaves the checkout on `main`, clean.

## Publish pre-branch ticket edits

Writing `branch:` or plan notes on `main` does not publish them: Git carries
uncommitted edits across a branch switch. Before switching, publish those
edits strictly, naming each edited file. The recipe resolves paths against
the current directory, which launch preserves, so anchor them at the checkout
root:

```sh
coga run publish-state "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/coga/tasks/<slug>.md"
git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all
```

Exit 0 means every named file is confirmed on control; any non-zero exit
(contract in [strict publication on
demand](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#strict-publication-on-demand))
is the stop signal. Use the status check only for dirty files you did not name,
and require it to be empty before switching. Do not fall back to calling the
sweep through a `python -c` one-liner: the sweep reports publication failures

# Reconcile work with moving main

The configured remote control branch (`origin/main` by default) is the source of
truth for shared repository state. A local checkout and the launch prompt are
snapshots; expect main to advance during a session. This applies to all agent
edits, including code, documentation, contexts, skills, workflows, tickets,
and bootstrap or ad-hoc work. A fresh launch does not guarantee a fresh handoff.

## Freshness checkpoints

Before editing, fetch current main and inspect changes relevant to the work,
including its governing instructions. Before publishing or handing off edits,
fetch again and reconcile against that tip. Read-only work needs no merge;
qualify conclusions tied to an older revision if relevant files changed.
Git-disabled or remote-less work cannot claim remote freshness; report that
limitation when handing off changes.

## Preserve both sides

Reconciliation preserves main's newer work and the still-needed local intent:

- For committed branch work, merge or rebase current main using the owning
  workflow's procedure ([code branch procedure](../SKILL.md#start-work-end)).
  Resolve straightforward conflicts yourself; a clean Git merge still needs
  inspection for changes in meaning or assumptions.
- For uncommitted edits, inspect the branch's committed changes as well as
  its staged and unstaged deltas and main's intervening changes. Preserve the
  dirty deltas in patches or file copies, including untracked files, and
  record the original branch HEAD. Verify those backups before clearing any
  dirty files. Restore tracked files and the index from the branch's own
  HEAD, merge or rebase current main, then reapply the still-needed dirty
  deltas onto the resulting branch, resolving conflicts there. Do not replace
  a feature file with main's version first: that also removes committed
  branch work which a working-tree patch does not contain.
- For a stale ticket publication or a handoff, preserve unpublished prose
  and blackboard notes before refreshing the ticket from control. Account
  for committed local intent as well as dirty edits; reconcile the intended
  changes onto control's current ticket while respecting CLI-owned lifecycle
  fields. This ticket-specific recovery is not a recipe for replacing code
  files with main's version. Never replay a transition merely because its
  publication failed; use the publication recovery described in the
  [handoff procedure](../SKILL.md#in-a-launched-session).

If any work already landed, prove that from history and content before dropping
the duplicate. Preserve the owning definition and reconcile dependent references.

## Sync a feature branch with control

Every Coga command run from a feature or detached checkout publishes the
ticket and log it changed to control and leaves those files dirty in that
checkout by design ([state publication](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#control-versus-feature-checkouts)).
A new ticket stays untracked. That dirt blocks `git merge` or `git rebase` of
control until it is dropped.

Drop it only when every dirty or untracked file under the Coga and contexts
roots already equals control. Each such file must be a regular file whose
bytes (after clean filters) and mode equal the copy in the local
`<remote>/<control>` ref. A tracked file must also have no staged change.
`coga status` checks this against local refs (fetch first for a current
answer). When it holds, `coga status` prints the exact command, anchored to
the Git root, with paths quoted for the current shell. On POSIX it has this
shape, and any part with no paths is left out:

```bash
git --literal-pathspecs -C <root> checkout -- <tracked…> && rm -- <untracked…> && git -C <root> merge --no-edit <remote>/<control>
```

Native Windows PowerShell gets the same steps with `Remove-Item -LiteralPath`,
each nested in `if ($?) { … }`. `git merge --autostash` is not enough: it sets
aside tracked dirt, but an untracked ticket identical to control still aborts
the merge ("untracked working tree files would be overwritten"). Prefer merge
over rebase for a branch that is already pushed, so it needs no force-push.

When `coga status` instead lists files that differ, are staged, have another
mode, or are deleted, do not use the command. Publish differing routine state
(tickets, the log) first (`coga run publish-state`), then check again. A file
[held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
cannot be published from the branch: commit it on the branch for review, or
redo it on control. Otherwise reconcile those files by hand as in
[Preserve both sides](#preserve-both-sides).

## Verify and escalate

Inspect the combined diff and run checks appropriate to the affected work
after reconciliation. If publication reports that main moved again, repeat
the comparison against the new tip. Normal movement is not itself a blocker.
Escalate per session conduct when intent conflicts, ownership is unclear, or
access prevents reconciliation; identify the conflicting changes and the
decision or capability needed. Never choose main's entire file blindly,
discard unique work to silence sync, or bypass a publication or lifecycle
guard. These rules do not authorize taking over another task's dirty checkout
or crossing a human approval gate.

# Manual start, work, end

Part of [coga/checkouts](../SKILL.md), which owns the launched lifecycle and
which checkout each step starts in.

## Procedure

Use this when no `COGA_LAUNCH_RETURNS_CHECKOUT=1` witness is set — manual or
API sessions, megalaunch picks, exempt checkouts — and before editing in a
step whose runtime notice says launch set up no branch (manual policy, or a
control step that must exceptionally change code). The agent performs both
moves:

1. **Start check.** `git fetch origin main`, then require HEAD on `main`, a
   clean tree with Coga state included, and a successful `git merge
   --ff-only origin/main`. Launch regenerates the ignored
   `coga/.agent-skills/` view; a repo initialized before `coga init` wrote
   that ignore rule sees it as dirt — add `.agent-skills/` to
   `coga/.gitignore`, never commit it. Anything else — dirty files, another
   ticket's branch, a diverged `main` — means stop: ask the attending human,
   or `coga block` in a queue run. Do not work around an occupied checkout
   with a linked worktree, a control checkout, a stash, or a switch.
2. **Work.** Write ticket state (`branch:` under `## Dev` once created with
   `git branch <name>`, plan notes) on `main`, publish it (below), then
   switch to the feature branch and change code only; ticket edits made
   there are not published until the next sweep. A resumed branch is reused:
   switch to it and `git rebase` onto fetched `origin/main`.
3. **End.** Commit, push the branch (`git push -u origin <branch>`, or
   `--force-with-lease` after a rebase), then return:
   - `git fetch origin main`;
   - for every dirty path under the Coga roots, verify it is already on
     `origin/main` by the rules of
     [the launch boundary](../launch-boundary/SKILL.md) (`git diff --quiet origin/main -- <path>`;
     for `coga/log.md`, every added line is on `origin/main`) and discard it
     (`git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <path>`). `git diff`
     skips untracked files, so compare an untracked one with
     `git show origin/main:<path> | cmp - <path>` and delete it only when
     identical;
   - `git switch main`, then `git merge --ff-only origin/main`.

   If any dirty path under the Coga roots is *not* already on `origin/main`,
   or any other path is dirty, stop and escalate. A knowledge file the sweep
   [held for merge](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#held-for-merge-on-feature-checkouts)
   belongs in the branch's commit (or redone on `main`), not discarded. Never discard unpublished
   state. Then write the step's handoff on `main` and run `coga bump`, which
   publishes it. The session leaves the checkout on `main`, clean.

## Publish pre-branch ticket edits

Writing `branch:` or plan notes on `main` does not publish them: Git carries
uncommitted edits across a branch switch. Before switching, publish those
edits strictly, naming each edited file. The recipe resolves paths against
the current directory, which launch preserves, so anchor them at the checkout
root:

```sh
coga run publish-state "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/coga/tasks/<slug>.md"
git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all
```

Exit 0 means every named file is confirmed on control; any non-zero exit
(contract in [strict publication on
demand](../../state-publication/SKILL.md#strict-publication-on-demand))
is the stop signal. Use the status check only for dirty files you did not name,
and require it to be empty before switching. Do not fall back to calling the
sweep through a `python -c` one-liner: the sweep reports publication failures
without raising, and the shell's `python` often cannot import Coga at all. If
publication fails or the tree remains dirty, stop and escalate; do not switch,
stash, or commit the ticket edit on the feature branch. The same publication applies to a
sandbox clone's `worktree:` record in the primary checkout, before starting
work in the clone.

name: code/with-review
description: Code change implemented by the main agent, then reviewed by its configured peer before a PR is opened for the human's final review.
steps:
  - name: implement
    assignee: agent
    requires: branch
    checkout: create-or-reuse
    skills:
      - code/implement
  - name: peer-review
    assignee: other-agent
    checkout: reuse-required
    skills:
      - code/peer-review
  - name: open-pr
    assignee: agent
    requires: pr
    checkout: control
    skills:
      - code/open-pr
  - name: review
    assignee: owner
    checkout: reuse-required
    skills:
      - code/address-pr-comments
---

## Before choosing this workflow

This workflow needs a second agent to review the code. Check `[agents.*]` in
`coga/coga.toml` and `coga.local.toml`. If only one agent is configured — or
three or more with no `peer =` on the main agent — use `code/with-self-review`
instead.

A step that declares `skills:` does **not** compose the `## <step>` section
below: Coga builds that step-specific layer from the declared skill files, and
the inline section is never read by the launched agent. The base prompt,
contexts, ticket-level skills, ticket body, and blackboard still compose
normally. Agent instructions therefore belong in the step's skills. Sections
here for a skilled step are human-facing framing only. Skill-less steps *do*
compose their section, so those bodies are load-bearing.

## Peer review by the other agent

The `implement` step derives its operator from the ticket's `agent:` main-agent
choice. The `peer-review` step declares `assignee: other-agent`, which resolves
to that main agent's configured peer. `coga bump` advances `step:` and the next
operator is derived from the frozen role; it never writes an assignment.
`open-pr` declares `agent` and routes back to the same main-agent choice.

With two configured agent types, `other-agent` infers the only peer with no
extra config. With three or more, set `peer = "<type>"` on the main agent's
`[agents.<type>]` table; the mapping is one-directional, so each main agent that
uses this workflow needs its own peer. An absent or ambiguous peer fails loud
rather than guessing.

An explicit launch override changes the executing agent without changing the
stored main agent or its peer. It can therefore make the same agent implement
and review a change. Peer selection alone does not prove independent authorship.

The `coga launch` supervisor auto-chains across these agent boundaries:
when a bump changes the derived operator (main → peer → main),
it launches the *next* agent as a fresh process under
the same supervisor — claude's REPL exits and codex's starts, or vice
versa. Each step is a clean session with a freshly composed prompt; it
only returns control to the human at the final `review` step (an
owner/human handoff), or on a terminal (`done`/`canceled`), `paused`, or
`blocked` state.

## implement

Agent step, owned by the `code/implement` skill. Launch creates or reuses the
recorded branch before the agent starts (`coga/checkouts`). The step declares
`requires: branch`, so `coga bump` refuses to advance until `branch:` is
recorded under `## Dev` in the ticket copy of the checkout the bump runs from.

## peer-review

Other-agent step, owned by the `code/peer-review` skill: the main agent's
configured peer reviews the branch diff, applies must-fix findings, freshens
the branch, and prepares `## PR` before the mechanical `open-pr` step.

Older frozen snapshots of this workflow declare no step skill, so they compose
this section instead. In that case, read and follow the `code/peer-review`
skill — `coga/skills/code/peer-review/SKILL.md` when present, else the
installed bundled copy — as if it were composed here. Peer selection alone
does not prove independent authorship; that skill says what to record.

## open-pr

Agent step, owned by the `code/open-pr` skill: `coga open-pr <slug>` pushes the
recorded branch, opens (or readies) the PR, and writes `pr:` back under
`## Dev`. It declares `requires: pr`, so `coga bump` holds the step until that
line exists.

The command is deterministic and has no judgment of its own, which is why the
preceding `peer-review` step is the one that authors the PR body and rebases the
branch.

## review

Owner-controlled gate. The human reviews the open PR on GitHub; the peer-review
pass has already applied its must-fix findings, so the diff is the post-review
state. The human decides whether to edit, request changes, push fixes, or merge.
An agent launched to assist here runs the `code/address-pr-comments` skill,
which carries the do-not-merge and do-not-bump rules for that assist.

After the human merges, the `autoclose-merged` recurring sweep marks the task
`done` on its next run (≤24h); `coga bump` closes it immediately.

`done` is not the end of the ticket. When the sweep closes it, the sweep also
disposes of the feature branch (and any leftover recorded worktree) recorded
under `## Dev`, but only what the shared checkout proofs show is safe to
remove; a `coga bump` close disposes of nothing. The closing act is still the
owner's — once the ticket is `done`, run `coga retire <slug>`. Retire runs the
same proofs on whatever checkout remains, then deletes the done ticket with no
agent: its learning already landed with the merged PR. The packaged
`bootstrap/retire/ticket.md` owns that procedure, and the
`coga/checkout-cleanup` context owns what the shared proofs prove, preserve,
and record for later sweeps.

name: coga/knowledge
description: The permanent authoring rule for Coga knowledge — which surface owns a fact, one owner per fact, links never load content, when to attach versus cite a topic, and the topic size review policy.
---

# Where knowledge lives

Every fact has exactly one owning file; when two copies disagree, the owner
is right. Choose the owner by what the knowledge is:

| Knowledge | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Shared facts and contracts: behavior, invariants, edge cases, product intent used across capabilities | a local topic under the configured contexts root (`<ref>/SKILL.md`), or the package owner of a shipped topic |
| Reusable process: how to do a thing | a skill (`coga/skills/<ref>/SKILL.md` or bundled) |
| One ticket-defined capability's behavior and procedure | its command ticket (`bootstrap/<name>/ticket.md`) or recurring template (`recurring/<name>/ticket.md`) |
| Maintenance procedures specific to that capability | supporting files beside its persistent ticket, linked for reading when needed |
| Per-ticket field guide: a summary carried by new tickets that links the owning topics | inline ticket template (`src/coga/resources/ticket.md`) |
| One task's temporary working state | that ticket's blackboard ([coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md)) |
| Execution history | `coga/log.md`, written only by CLI commands |
| Dated evidence, completed investigations, archived proposals, and other retired history | the repo's dated archive, outside the contexts root |

Humans and agents read the same owning file. Do not keep a short agent
rendition beside a longer human one: that is two owners of one fact, and the
copies drift independently. For shared facts, pick the topic whose subject
already covers the neighbouring facts; when two fit, the more narrowly
attached one wins, because the fact then costs tokens only where it is needed.

Durability alone does not make a document a context. Command tickets and
recurring templates persist; their individual executions and period tasks do
not. Keep a job's contract with the job: phone-home owns its snapshot boundary,
and Dream owns its phase order. Extract shared facts into a context and
reusable procedures into a skill when other capabilities need them.

Keep maintenance instructions separate from instructions for each run. A
template may link a sibling runbook, but recurring creation copies only
`ticket.py`, not supporting Markdown. Name the persistent template path when
directing a period to a supporting file; do not assume it is beside that
period's ticket. Skills and runbooks remain readable documentation for humans.

An owner decision *not* to act ("we looked at X and chose not to do it") is
product intent, so it belongs with X's standing owner: the shared topic, skill,
command ticket or recurring template, never only the temporary task that
recorded it. The lifecycle retires work tickets and period tasks; a decision
left in one gets re-raised. State what was declined, why, and what would reopen it.

The same retirement breaks links. Retro and `coga delete` remove a ticket
without repairing inbound references, so a topic that names a ticket by path
as the owner of an open question dangles once it retires. Point durable
surfaces at the question's standing owner, not at the transient ticket working
it, and grep for inbound references to a slug before it retires.

## Narrative links, never restates

An index, README, overview, or neighbouring topic may summarize and link to
the owner, but carries no specification-grade detail: no ordered lists, exact
names, counts or field lists that can drift on their own. "Launch stacks
conduct before task material, ticket last; the order is in
`coga/prompt-composition`" is a summary; copying the layer list is a second
specification. Command semantics live with their owning capability. A command
ticket or recurring template owns its own behavior (`bootstrap/retire/ticket.md`
owns `coga retire`); rules several jobs share stay in a topic the ticket links.
`coga/cli` is an index, and installed `coga <cmd> --help` is the syntax authority.

**Sync rule.** A PR that changes an owner greps other surfaces for the fact
and fixes or deletes any restatement in the same PR. No test enforces this
across surfaces; the authoring rule is the enforcement and Dream's knowledge
scan is the backstop. A shipped definition has one committed owner, its
package copy; a repo copy of the same ref is a deliberate local override, a
separate artifact, not a second owner to keep in sync. `CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` load in every agent session, so they carry pointers plus only the
rules needed outside `coga launch`, never an owning statement.

## Links do not load content

Composition includes attached refs only
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)). A markdown link
in a topic, skill, or ticket is navigation: the agent reads the target only if
it chooses to open the file, subject to that repo’s access rules. So an
overview does not bring in its children. Knowledge a step requires must be
attached explicitly by ref or named as a required read in the task or skill;
a navigation link alone does neither.

## Attach or cite

Choose from the two audiences defined in
[context layout](../context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences): user topics
under `coga/` support operating Coga in adopting repos; the local
Coga-dev set supports developing Coga itself. Select by the task's need,
then apply the attach-or-cite test below. A shipped instruction must resolve
its required knowledge from the user set; a development link is optional
navigation, never a dependency.

For a job-owned contract or supporting file, name its persistent path and the
sections to read in the task's `## Context`. Invoke a reusable skill by ref.
Do not recreate either as a context just to put it in `contexts:`.

`contexts:` is one ticket-wide list, composed whole into every launch of
every step. Decide per ticket across all planned steps:

- **Attach** when a step must have the facts without being told to look:
  its correctness depends on rules spread across the topic, or the author
  cannot predict which facts it will hit. Test: would a launched step go
  wrong if this were absent from the prompt?
- **Cite** when steps need a few identifiable facts from a topic that is
  large relative to the rest of the prompt, or when the ticket will *edit*
  that topic (it gets read first anyway).

Measure relative size at authoring time with `approx_tokens` from
`coga launch --prompt-report`, which skips the state sweep, so a trial
`contexts:` edit stays local; do not edit lifecycle frontmatter to measure,
and do not quote sizes (they go stale). No topic is
always-attach or always-cite.

A cite is one sentence in `## Context` naming the ref and path, saying it is
cited rather than attached, and naming the sections to read, followed by the
facts the step needs, cited as module plus symbol. Do not justify it by size.
The copied facts are a snapshot for that ticket, never a second owner. Citing
does not relax the sync rule: a ticket that changes behavior a cited topic
owns updates that topic and its dependent references in the same PR.

## Topic size review policy

Each topic is a directory holding `SKILL.md` with only `name` and a
one-sentence `description` stating its scope. Targets: 60 to 160 lines and
500 to 1,500 tokens (ceil(chars/4), frontmatter included); overview topics at
most 1,000 tokens. A topic over 200 lines, 10,000 bytes, or 2,500 tokens is
reviewed for a split into narrower leaves in its namespace, so tickets can
attach only the contract they need. An exception needs a recorded reason,
written in the oversized topic itself as one closing `Size exception:`
sentence saying why it stays whole. A reason kept only on a ticket
blackboard or in a PR leaves with them, and the next reader who measures the
topic cannot tell a decision from drift.

and record for later sweeps.
---
name: coga/knowledge
description: The permanent authoring rule for Coga knowledge — which surface owns a fact, one owner per fact, links never load content, when to attach versus cite a topic, and the topic size review policy.
---

# Where knowledge lives

Every fact has exactly one owning file; when two copies disagree, the owner
is right. Choose the owner by what the knowledge is:

| Knowledge | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Shared facts and contracts: behavior, invariants, edge cases, product intent used across capabilities | a local topic under the configured contexts root (`<ref>/SKILL.md`), or the package owner of a shipped topic |
| Reusable process: how to do a thing | a skill (`coga/skills/<ref>/SKILL.md` or bundled) |
| One ticket-defined capability's behavior and procedure | its command ticket (`bootstrap/<name>/ticket.md`) or recurring template (`recurring/<name>/ticket.md`) |
| Maintenance procedures specific to that capability | supporting files beside its persistent ticket, linked for reading when needed |
| Per-ticket field guide: a summary carried by new tickets that links the owning topics | inline ticket template (`src/coga/resources/ticket.md`) |
| One task's temporary working state | that ticket's blackboard ([coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md)) |
| Execution history | `coga/log.md`, written only by CLI commands |
| Dated evidence, completed investigations, archived proposals, and other retired history | the repo's dated archive, outside the contexts root |

Humans and agents read the same owning file. Do not keep a short agent
rendition beside a longer human one: that is two owners of one fact, and the
copies drift independently. For shared facts, pick the topic whose subject
already covers the neighbouring facts; when two fit, the more narrowly
attached one wins, because the fact then costs tokens only where it is needed.

Durability alone does not make a document a context. Command tickets and
recurring templates persist; their individual executions and period tasks do
not. Keep a job's contract with the job: phone-home owns its snapshot boundary,
and Dream owns its phase order. Extract shared facts into a context and
reusable procedures into a skill when other capabilities need them.

Keep maintenance instructions separate from instructions for each run. A
template may link a sibling runbook, but recurring creation copies only
`ticket.py`, not supporting Markdown. Name the persistent template path when
directing a period to a supporting file; do not assume it is beside that
period's ticket. Skills and runbooks remain readable documentation for humans.

An owner decision *not* to act ("we looked at X and chose not to do it") is
product intent, so it belongs with X's standing owner: the shared topic, skill,
command ticket or recurring template, never only the temporary task that
recorded it. The lifecycle retires work tickets and period tasks; a decision
left in one gets re-raised. State what was declined, why, and what would reopen it.

The same retirement breaks links. Retro and `coga delete` remove a ticket
without repairing inbound references, so a topic that names a ticket by path
as the owner of an open question dangles once it retires. Point durable
surfaces at the question's standing owner, not at the transient ticket working
it, and grep for inbound references to a slug before it retires.

## Narrative links, never restates

An index, README, overview, or neighbouring topic may summarize and link to
the owner, but carries no specification-grade detail: no ordered lists, exact
names, counts or field lists that can drift on their own. "Launch stacks
conduct before task material, ticket last; the order is in
`coga/prompt-composition`" is a summary; copying the layer list is a second
specification. Command semantics live with their owning capability. A command
ticket or recurring template owns its own behavior (`bootstrap/retire/ticket.md`
owns `coga retire`); rules several jobs share stay in a topic the ticket links.
`coga/cli` is an index, and installed `coga <cmd> --help` is the syntax authority.

**Sync rule.** A PR that changes an owner greps other surfaces for the fact
and fixes or deletes any restatement in the same PR. No test enforces this
across surfaces; the authoring rule is the enforcement and Dream's knowledge
scan is the backstop. A shipped definition has one committed owner, its
package copy; a repo copy of the same ref is a deliberate local override, a
separate artifact, not a second owner to keep in sync. `CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` load in every agent session, so they carry pointers plus only the
rules needed outside `coga launch`, never an owning statement.

## Links do not load content

Composition includes attached refs only
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)). A markdown link
in a topic, skill, or ticket is navigation: the agent reads the target only if
it chooses to open the file, subject to that repo’s access rules. So an
overview does not bring in its children. Knowledge a step requires must be
attached explicitly by ref or named as a required read in the task or skill;
a navigation link alone does neither.

## Attach or cite

Choose from the two audiences defined in
[context layout](../context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences): user topics
under `coga/` support operating Coga in adopting repos; the local
Coga-dev set supports developing Coga itself. Select by the task's need,
then apply the attach-or-cite test below. A shipped instruction must resolve
its required knowledge from the user set; a development link is optional
navigation, never a dependency.

For a job-owned contract or supporting file, name its persistent path and the
sections to read in the task's `## Context`. Invoke a reusable skill by ref.
Do not recreate either as a context just to put it in `contexts:`.

`contexts:` is one ticket-wide list, composed whole into every launch of
every step. Decide per ticket across all planned steps:

- **Attach** when a step must have the facts without being told to look:
  its correctness depends on rules spread across the topic, or the author
  cannot predict which facts it will hit. Test: would a launched step go
  wrong if this were absent from the prompt?
- **Cite** when steps need a few identifiable facts from a topic that is
  large relative to the rest of the prompt, or when the ticket will *edit*
  that topic (it gets read first anyway).

Measure relative size at authoring time with `approx_tokens` from
`coga launch --prompt-report`, which skips the state sweep, so a trial
`contexts:` edit stays local; do not edit lifecycle frontmatter to measure,
and do not quote sizes (they go stale). No topic is
always-attach or always-cite.

A cite is one sentence in `## Context` naming the ref and path, saying it is
cited rather than attached, and naming the sections to read, followed by the
facts the step needs, cited as module plus symbol. Do not justify it by size.
The copied facts are a snapshot for that ticket, never a second owner. Citing
does not relax the sync rule: a ticket that changes behavior a cited topic
owns updates that topic and its dependent references in the same PR.

## Topic size review policy

Each topic is a directory holding `SKILL.md` with only `name` and a
one-sentence `description` stating its scope. Targets: 60 to 160 lines and
500 to 1,500 tokens (ceil(chars/4), frontmatter included); overview topics at
most 1,000 tokens. A topic over 200 lines, 10,000 bytes, or 2,500 tokens is
reviewed for a split into narrower leaves in its namespace, so tickets can
attach only the contract they need. An exception needs a recorded reason,
written in the oversized topic itself as one closing `Size exception:`
sentence saying why it stays whole. A reason kept only on a ticket
blackboard or in a PR leaves with them, and the next reader who measures the
topic cannot tell a decision from drift.

---
name: coga/lifecycle
description: The two per-ticket state machines — status (whether work happens) and step (where in the frozen workflow) — with the single writer for each transition, blocking and blocked resume, bump and human rewind, cancellation rules, and the read-only `coga status` triage views.
---

# Ticket lifecycle

Each ticket has two independent state machines, and each state change has
one shared writer. Workflow shape and routing are
[coga/workflows](../workflows/SKILL.md).

## Status: whether work happens

Values: `draft`, `active`, `in_progress`, `paused`, `blocked`, and the
terminal outcomes `done` and `canceled`.

| Transition | Writer | Allowed from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| create `draft` | `coga create` (ignores `default_status`) | — |
| `active` | `coga mark active` | `draft`, `paused` |
| `in_progress` | `coga launch`, as script or agent work begins | `active` |
| `paused` | `coga mark paused` (keeps `step:`) | `active`, `in_progress` |
| `done` | `coga mark done`, or final-step `coga bump` (clears `step:`) | `active`, `in_progress` |
| `canceled` | `coga mark canceled --message <reason>` (clears `step:`) | any non-terminal |
| `blocked` | `coga block --task <ref> --reason ...` (keeps `step:`) | `active`, `in_progress`, `blocked` |
| `blocked → active` | `coga unblock` (keeps `step:`; on `in_progress` or a paused `recurring/` period it only resolves asks) | `blocked` |

Every writer above except launch decides from the ticket reconciled with
freshly fetched control, not this checkout's possibly stale copy: a terminal
control copy cannot be reopened by a stale `mark active`, pause, or block, and
owner and `requires:` gates are rechecked there
([prepared ticket transactions](../state-publication/SKILL.md#prepared-ticket-transactions)).

Launching is itself the
readiness signal: `coga launch` performs `mark active` inline on a `draft` or
`paused` ticket before flipping it to `in_progress`. Activation refuses a
ticket with no workflow, empty required extension fields, or unsynthesized
pre-launch authoring notes on the blackboard
([coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md)); first activation also fills
`agent:` and freezes a bare workflow ref ([coga/tickets](../tickets/SKILL.md)).
Tickets without a workflow move through statuses only via `coga mark`.

For an ordinary managed agent launch, activation and start are prepared in
memory and published as the final `in_progress` ticket with checkout linkage
and the launch audit. Their distinct audit events remain ordered; there is
no separately published intermediate `active` state. Standalone commands and
strict queue/recurring callers keep their own immediate transitions.
[Launch publication boundaries](../state-publication/launch-boundaries/SKILL.md)
owns the accounting; [checkout preparation](../checkouts/launch-boundary/SKILL.md)
owns refusal and retained-state recovery.

- `--message` adds an FYI to active/paused/done notifications; for canceled
  it is the required audit reason, appended to `coga/log.md`. Cancellation
  leaves the body and blackboard (including open blocker text) untouched.
- `done` and `canceled` are terminal: launch refuses them and nothing
  reactivates a canceled ticket. The one exception is `coga recurring
  --force`, which reactivates a `done` recurring period task
  ([coga/recurring/scheduling](../recurring/scheduling/SKILL.md#variants)). A terminal transition deletes no branch or
  checkout. The ticket's owned branches are cleaned up later by `coga retire`
  and each clone's daily branch sweep, so nothing disappears beneath the
  session that finished it. `coga retire` then removes the ticket: a done one
  is deleted with no retro agent, because its positive learning landed in its
  merged PR; a canceled one goes through Retro first, which extracts the
  cancellation reason and any other negative learning
  ([coga/checkout-cleanup/terminal-owners](../checkout-cleanup/terminal-owners/SKILL.md)).
  `mark done --force` / final-step `bump --force` finish a `direct/body`
  ticket while acknowledging product code stranded off the control branch.
- **Convention: `done` means the work landed; `canceled` means it did not.**
  Mark a ticket `done` only when the change its `## Description` scoped
  reached the control branch; work that is abandoned, superseded, or left
  stranded off the control branch ends `canceled`, with the reason. The CLI
  does not verify this, and `mark done --force` / final-step `bump --force`
  override its stranded-code guard, so the operator upholds the convention.
  `coga retire` relies on it: a done ticket is deleted with no Retro pass,
  so a ticket whose work did not land must be canceled to keep its learning.
- A terminal transition is a verdict about the ticket, never a repair of
  validator output. "Clears a validate error" is not a cancellation reason:
  cancelling parked drafts is the cheapest route to a green gate and trades
  the record of intent for an exit code.
- A cancellation that records an owner decision *not* to act is a verdict
  worth keeping, and the ticket is not where it lives: land it in the topic
  [coga/knowledge](../knowledge/SKILL.md) names, before or with the cancel,
  and let the cancellation reason point there. Dream's knowledge scan is the
  backstop for one that did not land.

## Blocking and resume

`coga block` appends the ask under `## Blockers`, sets `blocked`, logs and
syncs, notifies the owner live, and ends a launched session. The reason
should be answerable from `coga status --blocked` alone.

`coga unblock <ref> --answer "..."` marks each open ask `- [x]` with a
`resolved:` line and returns the task to `active` at the same step; without
`--answer` it prompts after showing the asks. On an `in_progress` ticket with
open asks it only resolves them. On a `paused` recurring period with open asks
it also only resolves them: the period stays `paused`, and the next sweep or
named launch resumes it with the answer on its blackboard
([recurring scheduling](../recurring/scheduling/SKILL.md#admission-and-unfinished-runs)).
Any other paused ticket is refused. `coga unblock --all` walks every blocked task,
prompting per task (blank skips; `--answer` is rejected) and ends with an
`Unblocked N, skipped M` summary.

An **interactive** (TTY) launch resumes a blocked ticket inline
(`blocked → active → in_progress`, step preserved) and composes the
resolve-or-re-block preamble ([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)).
If any resumed phase, including a `ticket.py` that fails, pauses, closes or
advances, exits before an answer is recorded, launch returns the ticket to
`blocked`, restoring the original step and routing inputs if a terminal
transition cleared them; an invalid baseline fails closed. TTY-less launches
refuse a blocked ticket until `coga unblock` records an answer.

## Step: where in the workflow

`step:` is `N (step-name)`, owned entirely by `coga bump`.

- Bare `coga bump <ref>` requires `in_progress`, checks the leaving step's
  `requires:` gate, and advances one step, or on the final step delegates to
  `mark_done`. A supervised bump whose session was composed for a step
  other than the one reconciled with control refuses as stale context. A
  workflow-less ticket is refused with a pointer to `coga mark done`. `--message` rides the transition notification. A forward
  bump from a step with a usable `## Dev` `branch:` warns on stderr (never
  blocks) about stranded ticket writes; see
  [coga/checkouts](../checkouts/SKILL.md).
- `--to` / `--backward` is a **human** rewind; agents inside a supervised
  launch are refused (`COGA_SUPERVISED`). It is recovery when a step went
  wrong but the ticket's premise still holds: because status and blackboard
  are untouched, everything learned stays. When the premise itself turns out
  wrong, the usual move is not a rewind:
  cancel the ticket with its reason, update the context that owns the fact,
  and open a new ticket. It repositions only: accepts
  `active`, `in_progress`, `paused`, never changes
  status, and derives the target operator without persisting it. From
  `active`/`paused` it must target an agent step (an owner step could not be
  resumed or bumped); `in_progress` may target either. It refuses `blocked`
  (unblock first) and terminal tickets. It moves backward from the step
  reconciled with control. If its guarded publication is not confirmed, the local mutation is left for inspection: reconcile the checkout
  with control before another mutating command, push, or merge.

Pausing preserves the step; cancellation clears it.

## Triage: `coga status`

A pure read: no mutation, no network. It lists live tasks; `--all` adds
terminal ones with separate counts. `coga status <dir>` limits to a subtree,
`--no-recurse` to one level, `--dirs` lists plain directories instead; an
unknown directory fails listing those that exist. `updated` comes from the
task's last `coga/log.md` line, falling back to the last commit touching its
files (or `-` without git). `--blocked` shows one row per open ask on
`status: blocked` tasks. When the view covers `tasks/recurring/`, a one-line
`Recurring` footer summarizes templates, due counts and load errors (full view:
`coga recurring list`, [coga/recurring](../recurring/SKILL.md)).

## Dependencies and supersession

A dependency is an open blocker ask on the **dependent** ticket:
`coga block --task <B> --reason "Depends on <A>: <what B needs from it>"`.
Use A's exact path-qualified slug (for example `v2/some-ticket`), as a whole
token, not its title or a partial slug. B must be active, in_progress, or
blocked; activate a draft first. This uses the existing blocker mechanism:
status and reminders show the ask, and the
[megalaunch dependency drain](../megalaunch/SKILL.md#dependency-drain) resolves
each dependency ask only when its exact named task is `done` or was seen
earlier in that run and has since been retired. With multiple dependencies,
satisfied asks resolve individually; unfinished dependencies and unrelated
human asks stay open, and B stays `blocked` while any ask remains. If an ask
names multiple known task refs, all must be finished before that ask resolves.
An explicit human `coga unblock` answer still resolves all open asks in one
transition. This is not a general dependency graph or a `dependencies:` field,
and cancellation does not count as completion.

When a newer ticket supersedes an older one, use
`coga mark canceled <old> --message "Superseded by <new>"`, with the successor's
exact path-qualified slug. The cancellation reason starts with `Superseded by `;
an optional date or explanation may follow. Cancellation removes the old ticket
from live queues, clears its step, and keeps its body and blackboard as history.
There is no separate `superseded` status. Leaving the replaced ticket paused or
draft keeps it live. If file readers need the pointer, open `## Context` with
**Superseded by `<new>` (<date>).** as a courtesy copy of the logged reason.
A superseded design within one ticket follows
[coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md#superseded-designs).

"""`coga status` — one line per task in the repo.

Thin Typer head: the directory operand + flag surface and error→exit
translation live here; the render itself is `coga.views.render_status`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys

import typer

from coga.config import ConfigError, load_config
from coga.tasks import UnknownDirectoryError
from coga.views import ORDER_BY_ALIASES, ORDER_BY_CHOICES, ViewError, render_status


def status(
    directory: str | None = typer.Argument(
        None,
        metavar="[DIR]",
        help=(
            "Show only tasks under `tasks/<DIR>/` (a directory path, nested "
            "ones included, e.g. `marketing` or `marketing/social`). Omit to "
            "show every task; add --no-recurse to show only the top level."
        ),
    ),
    no_recurse: bool = typer.Option(
        False,
        "--no-recurse",
        help=(
            "List only tasks sitting directly in the directory, none from "
            "sub-directories. With no DIR, shows the tasks directly under "
            "tasks/ (the top-level slice)."
        ),
    ),
    order_by: str = typer.Option(
        "updated",
        "--order-by",
        "-o",
        help=(
            f"Sort column. One of: {', '.join(ORDER_BY_CHOICES)} "
            f"(aliases: {', '.join(ORDER_BY_ALIASES)}). `operator` sorts the "
            "column derived from each ticket's current workflow step — it is a "
            "read-only view, not an assignment."
        ),
    ),
    reverse: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--reverse", "-r", help="Reverse sort order."
    ),
    show_all: bool = typer.Option(
        False,
        "--all",
        "-a",
        help="Include terminal `done` and `canceled` tasks (hidden by default).",
    ),
    dirs: bool = typer.Option(
        False,
        "--dirs",
        "-d",
        help=(
            "List the plain (non-task) directories under tasks/ instead of the "
            "tasks themselves, one path per line. Honors DIR (sub-dirs of that "
            "directory) and --no-recurse (only the immediate level)."
        ),
    ),
    blocked: bool = typer.Option(
        False,
        "--blocked",
        help="Show only blocked tickets, expanding every open blocker ask.",
    ),
) -> None:
    """Show tasks in the repo."""
    try:
        cfg = load_config(require_user=False)
    except ConfigError as exc:
        _bail(str(exc))

    try:
        render_status(
            cfg,
            directory=directory,
            no_recurse=no_recurse,
            order_by=order_by,
            reverse=reverse,
            show_all=show_all,
            dirs=dirs,
            blocked=blocked,
        )
    except (ViewError, UnknownDirectoryError) as exc:
        _bail(str(exc))


def _bail(msg: str) -> None:
    typer.secho(msg, fg=typer.colors.RED, err=True)
    sys.exit(2)

name: coga/blackboard
description: The writer's contract for a ticket blackboard — locating the fence, scoping edits, live sections and superseded designs, the draft-activation readiness check, size limits and their remedy, and safe concurrent writes. Attach to tickets whose work writes blackboards programmatically.
---

# Writing to a ticket blackboard

The blackboard is everything below the `<!-- coga:blackboard -->` fence in a
ticket: working memory shared by human and agent and carried between
stateless sessions. Its live state is composed into every launch
([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)); `coga/log.md`,
written only by CLI commands, holds lifecycle history and is never composed.
Working state the next run must read goes here and stays small; history goes
in the log.

## The fence

The fence counts only as a whole line: no leading indentation, optional
trailing whitespace. Markdown is not parsed, so an own-line fence inside a
code block counts, while an inline mention does not.

- **Never locate the fence by substring** (`split`, `find`, `partition`,
  unanchored `grep`/`sed`): a quoted fence in prose truncates the body.
- **Exactly one fence.** Readers fail on zero or several. Bootstrap command
  tickets legitimately have none.
- **Scope each edit.** Compute every transform on the blackboard region, never
  on whole-file text, so a `## Heading` pattern cannot hit the body, and never
  reformat the YAML while writing below the fence.

What may be edited above the fence is owned by
[coga/tickets](../tickets/SKILL.md) (agents: `contexts` and body sections).

## Section regimes

Match the section's regime; do not invent a fourth.

- **Live state: rewrite in place.** One current value per named line. `## Dev`
  (`branch:`, `worktree:`, `pr:`) is canonical; its shape is in
  the ticket template's guide comment. Old values live in git.
- **Record: append, never delete.** `## Superseded designs` takes dated
  entries (shape [below](#superseded-designs);
  only an archive pointer composes). `## Blockers` takes one checkbox per ask;
  `coga unblock` marks it `- [x]` and appends `resolved:`. Blocker readers
  ignore fenced examples and superseded sections.
  The writer does not (known limitation, unfixed): when a real ask is open,
  `coga unblock` (`blackboard.resolve_open_blockers`) also flips `- [ ]`
  examples in fences and superseded sections and appends `resolved:` to
  them, so keep example blockers out of a blackboard that may be unblocked.
- **Authoring scratch: synthesize before launch.** `## Evaluator review`,
  `## Ticket authoring notes`, `## Proposals`. The `bootstrap/ticket` cleanup
  folds durable substance into the body; for a draft it keeps
  `## Superseded designs` and resets the rest to the stock placeholder; for a
  non-draft it removes only the authoring sections it used.

## Superseded designs

When a design changes, rewrite `## Description` and `## Context` to describe
current work, with live requirements under `###` subheadings. Other top-level
body sections do not compose. Move the abandoned plan below the blackboard
fence into one `## Superseded designs` section; append dated entries oldest
to newest:

```markdown
## Superseded designs

### YYYY-MM-DD — <abandoned direction>

Superseded by: <current direction or decision>
Reason: <why the ticket pivoted>

<prior plan, acceptance details, and evidence worth retaining>
```

Retain enough to understand or reconsider the old plan, with copied headings
at `####` or deeper inside each entry. Keep history in this single section,
not scattered under alternative headings or left only in Git; only the exact,
unindented `## Superseded designs` heading starts it. The body may carry one
short pointer when a reviewer needs it; keep current decisions and their
rationale in live notes. The prompt includes only a pointer to the stored
history.

## Draft-activation readiness

On first activation (`mark active` or launch auto-activation) Coga refuses a
draft whose blackboard still holds authoring scratch sections or a large
custom scratchpad, before anything is written or spawned; `coga validate`
reports the same error. The stock placeholder (resource `blackboard.md`, which
a repo may override under `<coga root>/resources/`) counts as empty. Merge
durable requirements into `## Description` / `## Context` first. A
`## Production notes` section marks remaining content as intentional launch
material and exempts it; `## Superseded designs` is excluded without
exempting other notes. Later reactivations and forced recurring reruns do not
recheck. An `## Evaluator review` written by a live workflow step is working
state for the next owner gate, not residue.

## Size and its remedy

`coga validate` (`large-blackboard`) and launch warn above 32 KiB of live
notes. When `coga launch --prompt-report` shows the blackboard as the
largest layer, do not delete history. Promote a file-form task to directory
form, move dated evidence into sibling attachments (`tasks/<slug>/<topic>.md`,
opening with an HTML comment naming the task and move date), and leave the
current handoff, worklist and verification with a pointer to each. Keep
`## Dev` and `## Blockers` in place, since CLI readers do not follow links.
Material several tickets cite belongs in an unattached context. Record the
before/after layer sizes on the blackboard. A moved section leaves a
same-named heading holding only the pointer, so references to it (an
evaluator review citing `## Design`) still resolve.

The remedy is for live tickets. A flagged `done` ticket is not trimmed: one
with no live recorded checkout is left to Dream's retro pass, and one with a
live checkout is retirement debt that `coga retire <slug>` disposes of and
deletes ([Dream template](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/recurring/dream/ticket.md) owns that split). A section a writer rewrites
every run (a recurring template's state, Dream's own per-run report) is not
trimmed by hand either: the next run overwrites the edit, and
[coga/period-task](../period-task/SKILL.md) says to touch only your own keys.
Route it to its owner as a decision (attachment, exemption, or accepted
warning).

## Publishing cleanup

Draft synthesis and live-ticket size cleanup publish as Coga state through
[state publication](../state-publication/SKILL.md). The owner can edit directly
on control or track the cleanup in a workflow without branch or PR gates.
Ticket bodies, blackboards, and sibling attachments stay out of code PRs.

## What later passes do to content

- A replaced live value leaves the section; git keeps it.
- A replaced design moves into the single `## Superseded designs` section;
  the body keeps at most a one-line pointer. Keep rationale still needed for
  current work in live notes.
- A resolved blocker keeps its ask.
- A period task's blackboard is deleted at Dream's retro cleanup: durable
  gotchas go under `## Gotchas` for extraction and last-run state goes on the
  parent template's blackboard ([coga/period-task](../period-task/SKILL.md)).

## Concurrent writers

There is no ownership mutex; divergent workers are visible and recoverable in
git ([coga/launch](../launch/SKILL.md)). A `ticket.py` or other program that
writes a blackboard uses `blackboard.update_blackboard_under_barrier`, which
refuses rather than overwrite an intervening edit. Read the region
immediately before writing, prefer section appends to whole-region rewrites,
and keep writes as small as the change. Parser and race details are in
[blackboard IO](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/docs/contexts/coga-dev/internals/blackboard-io/SKILL.md);
cross-checkout reconciliation is in [coga/sync](../sync/SKILL.md).

# Ticket lifecycle

Each ticket has two independent state machines, and each state change has
one shared writer. Workflow shape and routing are
[coga/workflows](../workflows/SKILL.md).

## Status: whether work happens

Values: `draft`, `active`, `in_progress`, `paused`, `blocked`, and the
terminal outcomes `done` and `canceled`.

| Transition | Writer | Allowed from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| create `draft` | `coga create` (ignores `default_status`) | — |
| `active` | `coga mark active` | `draft`, `paused` |
| `in_progress` | `coga launch`, as script or agent work begins | `active` |
| `paused` | `coga mark paused` (keeps `step:`) | `active`, `in_progress` |
| `done` | `coga mark done`, or final-step `coga bump` (clears `step:`) | `active`, `in_progress` |
| `canceled` | `coga mark canceled --message <reason>` (clears `step:`) | any non-terminal |
| `blocked` | `coga block --task <ref> --reason ...` (keeps `step:`) | `active`, `in_progress`, `blocked` |
| `blocked → active` | `coga unblock` (keeps `step:`; on `in_progress` or a paused `recurring/` period it only resolves asks) | `blocked` |

Every writer above except launch decides from the ticket reconciled with
freshly fetched control, not this checkout's possibly stale copy: a terminal
control copy cannot be reopened by a stale `mark active`, pause, or block, and
owner and `requires:` gates are rechecked there
([prepared ticket transactions](../state-publication/SKILL.md#prepared-ticket-transactions)).

Launching is itself the
readiness signal: `coga launch` performs `mark active` inline on a `draft` or
`paused` ticket before flipping it to `in_progress`. Activation refuses a
ticket with no workflow, empty required extension fields, or unsynthesized
pre-launch authoring notes on the blackboard
([coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md)); first activation also fills
`agent:` and freezes a bare workflow ref ([coga/tickets](../tickets/SKILL.md)).
Tickets without a workflow move through statuses only via `coga mark`.

For an ordinary managed agent launch, activation and start are prepared in
memory and published as the final `in_progress` ticket with checkout linkage
and the launch audit. Their distinct audit events remain ordered; there is
no separately published intermediate `active` state. Standalone commands and
strict queue/recurring callers keep their own immediate transitions.
[Launch publication boundaries](../state-publication/launch-boundaries/SKILL.md)
owns the accounting; [checkout preparation](../checkouts/launch-boundary/SKILL.md)
owns refusal and retained-state recovery.

- `--message` adds an FYI to active/paused/done notifications; for canceled
  it is the required audit reason, appended to `coga/log.md`. Cancellation
  leaves the body and blackboard (including open blocker text) untouched.
- `done` and `canceled` are terminal: launch refuses them and nothing
  reactivates a canceled ticket. The one exception is `coga recurring
  --force`, which reactivates a `done` recurring period task
  ([coga/recurring/scheduling](../recurring/scheduling/SKILL.md#variants)). A terminal transition deletes no branch or
  checkout. The ticket's owned branches are cleaned up later by `coga retire`
  and each clone's daily branch sweep, so nothing disappears beneath the
  session that finished it. `coga retire` then removes the ticket: a done one
  is deleted with no retro agent, because its positive learning landed in its
  merged PR; a canceled one goes through Retro first, which extracts the
  cancellation reason and any other negative learning
  ([coga/checkout-cleanup/terminal-owners](../checkout-cleanup/terminal-owners/SKILL.md)).
  `mark done --force` / final-step `bump --force` finish a `direct/body`
  ticket while acknowledging product code stranded off the control branch.
- **Convention: `done` means the work landed; `canceled` means it did not.**
  Mark a ticket `done` only when the change its `## Description` scoped
  reached the control branch; work that is abandoned, superseded, or left
  stranded off the control branch ends `canceled`, with the reason. The CLI
  does not verify this, and `mark done --force` / final-step `bump --force`
  override its stranded-code guard, so the operator upholds the convention.
  `coga retire` relies on it: a done ticket is deleted with no Retro pass,
  so a ticket whose work did not land must be canceled to keep its learning.
- A terminal transition is a verdict about the ticket, never a repair of
  validator output. "Clears a validate error" is not a cancellation reason:
  cancelling parked drafts is the cheapest route to a green gate and trades
  the record of intent for an exit code.
- A cancellation that records an owner decision *not* to act is a verdict
  worth keeping, and the ticket is not where it lives: land it in the topic
  [coga/knowledge](../knowledge/SKILL.md) names, before or with the cancel,
  and let the cancellation reason point there. Dream's knowledge scan is the
  backstop for one that did not land.

## Blocking and resume

`coga block` appends the ask under `## Blockers`, sets `blocked`, logs and
syncs, notifies the owner live, and ends a launched session. The reason
should be answerable from `coga status --blocked` alone.

`coga unblock <ref> --answer "..."` marks each open ask `- [x]` with a
`resolved:` line and returns the task to `active` at the same step; without
`--answer` it prompts after showing the asks. On an `in_progress` ticket with
open asks it only resolves them. On a `paused` recurring period with open asks
it also only resolves them: the period stays `paused`, and the next sweep or
named launch resumes it with the answer on its blackboard
([recurring scheduling](../recurring/scheduling/SKILL.md#admission-and-unfinished-runs)).
Any other paused ticket is refused. `coga unblock --all` walks every blocked task,
prompting per task (blank skips; `--answer` is rejected) and ends with an
`Unblocked N, skipped M` summary.

An **interactive** (TTY) launch resumes a blocked ticket inline
(`blocked → active → in_progress`, step preserved) and composes the
resolve-or-re-block preamble ([coga/prompt-composition](../prompt-composition/SKILL.md)).
If any resumed phase, including a `ticket.py` that fails, pauses, closes or
advances, exits before an answer is recorded, launch returns the ticket to
`blocked`, restoring the original step and routing inputs if a terminal
transition cleared them; an invalid baseline fails closed. TTY-less launches
refuse a blocked ticket until `coga unblock` records an answer.

## Step: where in the workflow

`step:` is `N (step-name)`, owned entirely by `coga bump`.

- Bare `coga bump <ref>` requires `in_progress`, checks the leaving step's
  `requires:` gate, and advances one step, or on the final step delegates to
  `mark_done`. A supervised bump whose session was composed for a step
  other than the one reconciled with control refuses as stale context. A
  workflow-less ticket is refused with a pointer to `coga mark done`. `--message` rides the transition notification. A forward
  bump from a step with a usable `## Dev` `branch:` warns on stderr (never
  blocks) about stranded ticket writes; see
  [coga/checkouts](../checkouts/SKILL.md).
- `--to` / `--backward` is a **human** rewind; agents inside a supervised
  launch are refused (`COGA_SUPERVISED`). It is recovery when a step went
  wrong but the ticket's premise still holds: because status and blackboard
  are untouched, everything learned stays. When the premise itself turns out
  wrong, the usual move is not a rewind:
  cancel the ticket with its reason, update the context that owns the fact,
  and open a new ticket. It repositions only: accepts
  `active`, `in_progress`, `paused`, never changes
  status, and derives the target operator without persisting it. From
  `active`/`paused` it must target an agent step (an owner step could not be
  resumed or bumped); `in_progress` may target either. It refuses `blocked`
  (unblock first) and terminal tickets. It moves backward from the step
  reconciled with control. If its guarded publication is not confirmed, the local mutation is left for inspection: reconcile the checkout
  with control before another mutating command, push, or merge.

Pausing preserves the step; cancellation clears it.

## Triage: `coga status`

A pure read: no mutation, no network. It lists live tasks; `--all` adds
terminal ones with separate counts. `coga status <dir>` limits to a subtree,
`--no-recurse` to one level, `--dirs` lists plain directories instead; an
unknown directory fails listing those that exist. `updated` comes from the
task's last `coga/log.md` line, falling back to the last commit touching its
files (or `-` without git). `--blocked` shows one row per open ask on
`status: blocked` tasks. When the view covers `tasks/recurring/`, a one-line
`Recurring` footer summarizes templates, due counts and load errors (full view:
`coga recurring list`, [coga/recurring](../recurring/SKILL.md)).

## Dependencies and supersession

A dependency is an open blocker ask on the **dependent** ticket:
`coga block --task <B> --reason "Depends on <A>: <what B needs from it>"`.
Use A's exact path-qualified slug (for example `v2/some-ticket`), as a whole
token, not its title or a partial slug. B must be active, in_progress, or
blocked; activate a draft first. This uses the existing blocker mechanism:
status and reminders show the ask, and the
[megalaunch dependency drain](../megalaunch/SKILL.md#dependency-drain) resolves
each dependency ask only when its exact named task is `done` or was seen
earlier in that run and has since been retired. With multiple dependencies,
satisfied asks resolve individually; unfinished dependencies and unrelated
human asks stay open, and B stays `blocked` while any ask remains. If an ask
names multiple known task refs, all must be finished before that ask resolves.
An explicit human `coga unblock` answer still resolves all open asks in one
transition. This is not a general dependency graph or a `dependencies:` field,
and cancellation does not count as completion.

When a newer ticket supersedes an older one, use
`coga mark canceled <old> --message "Superseded by <new>"`, with the successor's
exact path-qualified slug. The cancellation reason starts with `Superseded by `;
an optional date or explanation may follow. Cancellation removes the old ticket
from live queues, clears its step, and keeps its body and blackboard as history.
There is no separate `superseded` status. Leaving the replaced ticket paused or
draft keeps it live. If file readers need the pointer, open `## Context` with
**Superseded by `<new>` (<date>).** as a courtesy copy of the logged reason.
A superseded design within one ticket follows
[coga/blackboard](../blackboard/SKILL.md#superseded-designs).
